Solutions 1 and 2 are refuted by Solution 3's counterexample at n = 8, which I checked directly. Take H = SQS(8), the affine-plane system on 8 points with 14 blocks of size 4, so every triple lies in exactly one block and δ₃(H) = 1. Any 5-set F contains exactly one block B = F∖{u}. In any 5-cycle ordering, the two consecutive triples avoiding u both lie in B and have no other covering edge, so they cannot be assigned distinct hyperedges. Hence H has no Berge-C₅³, and the statement fails at n = 8. This forces n₀ ≥ 9, which rules out 6 and 7.

Solution 3's answer of 9 is consistent with this, but I did not verify that the statement holds for every n ≥ 9. The n = 9 case is unresolved, so my confidence is moderate.
